### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **2** documentable anchor(s).

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via INVALID_REQUEST (literal, a string literal in registerAuthRoutes))_
- `content/docs/api/metadata-api.mdx`  _(via INVALID_REQUEST (literal, a string literal in registerAuthRoutes))_
- `content/docs/automation/webhooks.mdx`  _(via INVALID_REQUEST (literal, a string literal in registerAuthRoutes))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/import-mappings.mdx`  _(via INVALID_REQUEST (literal, a string literal in registerAuthRoutes))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via INVALID_REQUEST (literal, a string literal in registerAuthRoutes))_
- `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx`  _(via INVALID_REQUEST (literal, a string literal in registerAuthRoutes))_
- `content/docs/ui/forms.mdx`  _(via INVALID_REQUEST (literal, a string literal in registerAuthRoutes))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via INVALID_REQUEST (literal, a string literal in registerAuthRoutes))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via INVALID_REQUEST (literal, a string literal in registerAuthRoutes))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-0.mdx`  _(via INVALID_REQUEST (literal, a string literal in registerAuthRoutes))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **19** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json eddffc3390cf7e2cb9fd39960abc7fef4c40c902` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8c8b065c6641e9a2e227f94dd3d991539f9d0460` — the merge of head `48857fcc67456e5da3f9169285a9e49784c820f9` into base `eddffc3390cf7e2cb9fd39960abc7fef4c40c902`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8c8b065c6641e9a2e227f94dd3d991539f9d0460 && git checkout 8c8b065c6641e9a2e227f94dd3d991539f9d0460
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin eddffc3390cf7e2cb9fd39960abc7fef4c40c902 48857fcc67456e5da3f9169285a9e49784c820f9 && git checkout -B drift-repro eddffc3390cf7e2cb9fd39960abc7fef4c40c902 && git merge --no-ff 48857fcc67456e5da3f9169285a9e49784c820f9

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json eddffc3390cf7e2cb9fd39960abc7fef4c40c902
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs eddffc3390cf7e2cb9fd39960abc7fef4c40c902` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `48857fcc67456e5da3f9169285a9e49784c820f9`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/oauth-register-application-type.test.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-oauth-application.object.ts + .changeset/24773-oauth-type-refusal.md, .changeset/24773-oauth-application-type.md, .changeset/24773-oauth-form-types.md, .changeset/24773-oauth-register-refusal-status.md (unedited, judged), .changeset/24813-adopt-orphans-readonly-package.md (the BREAKING-minor shape), scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs (`readArmToken`), and at the 18.0.0 tag commit `06cab4849`: the register route in auth-plugin.ts and the form's type options in sys-oauth-application.object.ts

Isolated contract review (narrowing face) of PR #25038 for card #24773, rendered 2026-10-21T04:48Z. Inputs: the card's body and all 18 comments (rulings D `6293344532`, 「甲」 `6292005854` and its amendment `6303865025`, the claim `6302570331` as widened for half 2c, every dev report and seat record); the PR body, its 6-file list and the net diff against the merge base `dfe60e3a0` (143+ / 56-); the check-runs on the head, read last. No path of the diff moved on `origin/main` since the merge base. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**1. The accept set of `POST /api/v1/auth/sys-oauth-application/register` (auth-plugin.ts `:3612`-`:3739` at the head) — right.**
- Order in the route: body read → `name` required → `redirectURLs` required and non-empty → the application-type branch (`:3661`-`:3679`) → `getApi()` and the 503 provider check → `createOAuthClient` → the catch that maps provider refusals to `OAUTH_REGISTER_FAILED` → 200.
- `type === 'web' || type === 'native'` is forwarded as `application_type` (`:3699`). `type === undefined` or `type === null` falls through to `applicationType = 'web'`. Every other present value, strings (`''` included) and non-strings alike, returns `c.json({ success: false, error: { code: 'INVALID_REQUEST', message } }, 400)` at `:3669` — before `getApi()` is awaited and before `createOAuthClient` is called, so nothing is stored and nothing is logged. The envelope is the one the route's own `name` / `redirectURLs` refusals use at `:3626`, `:3629`, `:3637`, and `INVALID_REQUEST` is a code the route already answered: no new error code, no new status.
- The warning branch half 2a added (`ctx.logger.warn` with `registeredAs: 'web'`) is removed, not kept beside the refusal. Right: the refusal replaces the loud half, as the amendment of 「甲」 says (rule 2: the warning half alone is no longer the 18.x deliverable).
- Placing the type refusal before the 503 "OIDC provider is not enabled" check matches the two request-shape refusals that already precede it; on a stack without the provider a malformed type is refused as malformed, which is the right order for a request-shape refusal.
- The accept set after this diff is exactly: `web`, `native`, and no type (absent or JSON `null`). Judged right against ruling D (an unknown type is refused loudly with 400, the silent coercion to `web` ends) and the amendment (the refusal ships in 18.x).

**2. The dev's reading that `null` is absent and `''` is present — right.**
- Ruling D and 裁后执行 (`6289866018`) refuse "an unknown type" (未知类型拒 400); the amendment re-times that refusal. Neither text names `null` or `''`, so the question is which values name a type.
- `''` is a present string that names no known type: under D it is an unknown type, and half 2a already put it in the warning branch (the loud half whose refusal the amendment ships now). Refusing it is the ruling as written.
- JSON `null` is the body's spelling of no value: half 2a read it as absent (no warning), the provider's own default is `web`, and the form's declared default is `web`. Refusing it would narrow past the set the loud half announced, i.e. past what D and the amendment cover. Keeping it as `web` is right.
- So the refused set equals exactly the set that warned at the merge base, which is the cleanest reading of "the refusal replaces the warning". Pinned both ways: `type: null` → 200 stored `web`, no warning (`:332`-`:336` of the test file); `''` → 400 `INVALID_REQUEST`, no provider call (the `REFUSED` table, `:347`).

**3. The message — right.**
- `shown` is `JSON.stringify(type.length > 64 ? type.slice(0, 64) + '…' : type)` for a string, else `(typeof type)` (`:3665`-`:3668`). So the message carries at most the value's first 64 characters (UTF-16 units; `JSON.stringify` escapes but never extends what is echoed), plus a single ellipsis that is not from the value, and names a non-string by its type (`(number)`, `(boolean)`, `(object)`). It names `'web'`, `'native'`, `http://localhost`, `http://127.0.0.1` and `http://[::1]`.
- Pinned at `:375`-`:390`: 64 `a` characters echoed, the tail `TAIL-NEVER-ECHOED` absent, the five subjects present, a short value named whole, `42` named `(number)`.

**4. The test file — the pins match the accept set.**
- Half 2a's pins remain unchanged: the two provider preconditions, `web` + loopback refused by the provider's web rule (`OAUTH_REGISTER_FAILED`, `invalid_redirect_uri`), `native` + `localhost` / `127.0.0.1` stored `native`, `native` + plain http on a non-loopback host refused by the body schema, `native` + `127.0.0.2` refused by the native rule, `web` + https stored `web`, no type → `web`.
- Added: `null` → `web`; seven refused values × https and loopback, each asserting 400, a clean ADR-0112 envelope, `INVALID_REQUEST`, zero provider calls (a pass-through `vi.spyOn` on the one api object `getApi()` hands out), zero new rows at driver level, zero `warn` and zero `error` calls; the message pin. `expectStoredAs` now also asserts exactly one provider call carrying the stored `application_type`, which pins the forwarding itself.

**5. The stored column — untouched, and the finding is routed.**
- `type: Field.select(['web', 'native', 'user-agent-based', 'public'], ...)` at `:449` and `public: Field.boolean(...)` at `:456` of sys-oauth-application.object.ts are byte-identical between the merge base and the head; the file's only hunk is the action's code comment (`:151`-`:164`, 8+ / 8-, same line count), whose new text states the 18.x refusal, the absent / `null` → `web` rule, and the stored-column readings as the card's half 2a and 2b reports measured them. No param, option, label or field changes.
- The PR's Acceptance notes carry both residual readings (the select declares `useragentbased` / `public` with no writer; legacy `user-agent-based` rows and 1.7.3's update paths, source reading only), marked "not narrowed here" and reported to the seat, and the seat's rework note `6307609026` names both as routed at ACCEPT. Right.

**6. The deliberate correction — confirmed, sentence by sentence.** BEFORE is read at the merge base (`git show dfe60e3a0:PATH`), AFTER at the head. The falsifying fact for every pair is item 1 above: a present type other than `web` / `native` answers 400 `INVALID_REQUEST`, nothing is stored, nothing is logged.

`.changeset/24773-oauth-application-type.md` (`@objectstack/plugin-auth`: patch, frontmatter unchanged). One bullet rewritten:
- BEFORE label "**Unchanged, with a warning.**" → AFTER "**Refused.**". The BEFORE label is falsified (neither unchanged nor warned); the AFTER label is true at the end of this release.
- Kept verbatim: "Any other type, including the form's `user-agent-based` and `public`, has no `application_type` in the provider." Still true (the provider's `application_type` is `web` | `native`). "The form's" reads against this entry's own FROM state, the four-option form, which the register-form entry in the same release retires; not falsified by this diff.
- BEFORE "It keeps today's outcome: registered and judged as `web`, with a client secret." → falsified: such a request is refused, no `web` client is issued, no secret is minted. AFTER "The register route refuses it with `400 INVALID_REQUEST` and registers nothing (this release's breaking entry for the route)." → true: the status, the code, the no-store and the cross-reference (this PR's own entry, same release) all hold.
- BEFORE "The server now logs one warning per such registration, naming the value." → falsified: the `warn` call is gone and the pins assert zero warnings. Removed, with no replacement needed: the AFTER sentence above states the whole outcome.
- Kept verbatim: "To use a loopback redirect URI, register the client as `native`." Still true and pinned.
- Every unedited sentence stays true: the title, the `Clause-②: no —` line, the FROM paragraph, the "**Now.**" bullet, and "**Unchanged.** No type at all is `web`. Refusals keep the codes and statuses they had: `400 OAUTH_REGISTER_FAILED` ..." (this diff adds a refusal before the provider and changes no existing code or status). No still-true sentence was lost.

`.changeset/24773-oauth-form-types.md` (`@objectstack/platform-objects`: patch, frontmatter unchanged). Three sentences changed:
- The `Clause-②` line. BEFORE "Clause-②: no (a form's offering: the register route still accepts every type value it accepted, and nothing on the server reads the action's param options, so no accept set or served shape moves)" → the clause "still accepts every type value it accepted" is falsified. AFTER "Clause-②: no (a form's offering: nothing on the server reads the action's param options, so this change moves no accept set or served shape; the register route's refusal of the other types is its own breaking entry in this release)" → true: the form change itself moves no accept set, and the narrowing is carried by this PR's entry. The value stays `no`, which is right for a form's offering. Read against `readArmToken` in scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs (`:280`-`:293`): the parenthetical's first word is `a`, not a widen / narrow word, so it is ordinary reasoning and the line's reading is unchanged; the Check Changeset job's notice annotation on this head counts exactly one declared-breaking changeset, this PR's own.
- BEFORE "The OAuth provider judges only `web` and `native`, so the register route registers the other two as `web`, with a client secret." → falsified. AFTER "The OAuth provider judges only `web` and `native`, and the register route refuses any other type with `400 INVALID_REQUEST`." → true at the end of this release ("any other type" reads as a present type; no type stays `web`, as the plugin-auth entries say).
- BEFORE "**Unchanged.** The register route accepts the same values as before, including `user-agent-based` and `public`." → falsified; removed. The bullet keeps "The stored `sys_oauth_application.type` column still lists all four values, so a row written under an earlier provider line keeps its value. The `public` column is unchanged." → both still true (item 5). Removing rather than rewriting is right: the refusal is stated in the corrected sentence above and in this PR's entry, and the label "Unchanged." still heads two true sentences.
- Every unedited sentence stays true: the title, the history sentence ("offered four application types"), "The form now offers Web and Native, and still defaults to Web.", the Redirect URLs help, the Application Type help, the translations line. No still-true sentence was lost.

`.changeset/24773-oauth-register-refusal-status.md` (unedited) holds no sentence this diff falsifies. Its FROM (provider refusals answered 500), its "**Now.**" (400 for `invalid_redirect_uri`, 401 for a missing session, the code stays `OAUTH_REGISTER_FAILED` with `details.upstreamError`), and its "**Unchanged.**" (a no-status throw stays 500, the body-schema refusal stays 400, "a `web` client still needs an `https` URI on a non-loopback host") all describe the catch block at `:3703`-`:3729`, which this diff does not touch; the new refusal comes before the provider is called, and the note's examples use `web`, an accepted type.

**7. This PR's own note, `.changeset/24773-oauth-type-refusal.md`, judged against 18.0.0 and against the end of this release.** The 18.0.0 state was read at the tag commit `06cab4849` (`@objectstack/plugin-auth@18.0.0` and `@objectstack/platform-objects@18.0.0` both point there): the route computed `safeType` from `allowedTypes = {web, native, user-agent-based}` else `'web'` and forwarded it as `type`, which the provider strips, so every client was judged and stored as `web`, with no warning; the form offered four types.
- Frontmatter `plugin-auth: minor`, `platform-objects: patch` — right (② below).
- Title "refuses an application type the OAuth provider does not judge with `400 INVALID_REQUEST`, where it registered it as a `web` client" — true of 18.0.0 (registered as `web`) and of the head (refused).
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing) — the register door accepted any type value and registered every one other than web / native as a web client with a secret; it now refuses each of those values with 400, so it accepts exactly web, native and no type.` — true: 18.0.0 accepted any value and registered the non-`web` / `native` ones as `web` (it also registered `native` as `web`, which this line does not deny and the Application Type entry covers); the head accepts exactly the three.
- The adr-0087 marker: `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` — right: no spec key, authorable spelling, object definition, stored shape or export moves; the remedy is a different request value. The marker's sentence that the form "already offers only Web and Native" is true at the end of this release, not of 18.0.0; it is the gate-read disposition reason inside a hidden comment, not a FROM statement. Nit, no change required.
- "**BREAKING** (a REST door's accept set narrows), shipped as `minor` under the launch-window convention" — the #24813 shape, as the amendment prescribes.
- The paragraph: the provider judges `web` and `native`; the door forwards the form's choice as `application_type` (end-of-release, present tense); "The door used to register such a request as a confidential `web` client, with a client secret and the web redirect-URI rule" — true of 18.0.0; "It now refuses the request instead." — true.
- **FROM:** "a request whose `type` is present and is neither `web` nor `native` (`user-agent-based`, `public`, any other string including the empty string, or a value that is not a string) answered `200` and stored a `web` client, or was refused by the web rule (`OAUTH_REGISTER_FAILED`) for a loopback redirect URI." — true of 18.0.0 for every listed value: `safeType` maps a non-string, `''`, `public` and any unknown string to `'web'`, and `user-agent-based` is stripped to `web` by the provider; an https redirect registered `web` (200), a loopback one was refused by the web rule with `OAUTH_REGISTER_FAILED`. The r3 removal of the warning phrase was right: 18.0.0 logged nothing. The r4 rewrite names no status, which is right (see the observation below).
- **TO:** 400, `INVALID_REQUEST`, the first 64 characters, both accepted types, the three loopback hosts, no provider call, nothing stored, no warning — each true of the head (items 1 and 3). For a non-string the message names the type rather than the value; the note's "names the value" is a slight simplification, not a false sentence.
- **Accepted:** `web` and `native` forwarded as `application_type` "(this release's Application Type entry)" — true at the end of this release and correctly not stated as the FROM (18.0.0 stored `native` as `web`).
- **Unchanged:** no `type` or `type: null` registers `web` — true in 18.0.0 (`null` is not a string → `'web'`) and at the head. "The other refusals keep their codes (their statuses are this release's refusal-status entry)" — the codes are untouched, and the statuses are pointed at the pending note, which ships in this release's CHANGELOG. "Clients already registered are not touched." — true: no row is read or written.
- **`@objectstack/platform-objects`:** comment only, ships in the package's JavaScript; "The form offers only Web and Native (this release's register-form entry)." — true at the end of this release, correctly cross-referenced rather than claimed of 18.0.0.
- **The fix for an integrator:** matches the provider's rule as pinned (`native` for loopback http, `web` for https on a non-loopback host, omitted type → `web`).
- Observation, no FAIL: the dev's r4 rationale says the loopback refusal "answered 500 in 18.0.0". The 18.0.0 tag commit `06cab4849` has half 1's merge `950f949a9` as an ancestor, and its register route already reads `resolveThrownHttpError(err, 500)`, so a build from that commit answers 400 there — while the 18.0.0 `CHANGELOG.md` of plugin-auth carries no #24773 entry and `.changeset/24773-oauth-register-refusal-status.md` is still pending at the tag and on `main` (the version-packages snapshot predates that merge). The card's own 500 was measured on 18.0.0-next.5, which predates the fix. The r4 sentence names no status, so it is true under either reading; the pending refusal-status note will describe, in this release's notes, a change already present in a tarball built from the 18.0.0 tag commit. For the seat, not this PR's.

### ② Semver level

- What the diff publishes: `@objectstack/plugin-auth` narrows one REST door's accept set (a present `type` other than `web` / `native` was accepted, now refused) — BREAKING under `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`; no ADR-0087 conversion carries it (no authored metadata moves), so under 「甲」 as amended (`6303865025`, rule 2) it ships now in 18.x as a BREAKING `minor` with `!` in the title, the BREAKING banner, and an adr-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` disposition — the `24813-adopt-orphans-readonly-package` shape, matched line for line. `@objectstack/platform-objects` publishes a changed `dist` JavaScript (esbuild keeps the comment text, per the dev's measured sha256 comparison; the package is not `private`), so a `patch` entry is right and `skip-changeset` does not apply.
- The changeset frontmatter (`plugin-auth: minor`, `platform-objects: patch`) matches that; no `major` is introduced. The two corrected notes keep their `patch` levels and their `Clause-②: no` lines, and are not re-read as breaking: the Check Changeset job's notice annotation on this head reads exactly one ADR-0087 exemption, on `.changeset/24773-oauth-type-refusal.md`.
- `Clause-②:` line — the PR body's `Clause-②: no (narrowing) — ...` and the changeset's line carry the same arm and the same reason, and match the half-2c dispatch's `Clause-② (2c): no (narrowing)`. A narrowing owes this record at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` before the queue, which is what this is.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none in any 2c round (`6307562409`, `6307878565`, `6308016949`, `6308135792`). Nothing to answer.
- Dev deviations, each answered: (a) the dogfood battery ran once at `3f934a772` and was not re-run after the merge of `main` `dfe60e3a0` or the prose rounds — accepted: that merge moved no path of this diff, r2-r4 are changeset prose only, and the head's `Dogfood Regression Gate` check-run is success; (b) `platform-objects` `patch` for a comment-only source change — right (②); (c) `''` refused, `null` kept — right (① 2); (d) an ellipsis after the 64th character where the warning cut silently — fine, the marker is not from the value and the pin asserts the tail never appears; (e) #24813 is an issue, the shape was read from its changeset file — confirmed against that file; (f) the PR was opened at `3f934a772` without re-merging, then merged `dfe60e3a0` in r2 — the net diff's paths have not moved on `origin/main` since that merge base, and the PR reads mergeable; (g) the throwaway probe file is not in the diff (6 files, none new under `src/` besides the edited test); (h) sibling-repo reads through owned refs and grep-only tarball reads — process notes, no surface breach; (i) r2's `Clause-②` parenthetical rewrite — verified against `readArmToken` (① 6); (j) r4's two extra phrase changes beyond the proposed one — judged right (① 7); (k) the adr-0087 marker's "already offers" left as written — accepted as a nit (① 7).
- File surface of the widened claim `6302570331` (2c): auth-plugin.ts's application-type branch only — the file's single hunk is `:3647`-`:3680`; sys-oauth-application.object.ts's code comment only — same line count, select and `public` byte-identical; test files under `plugin-auth/src/`; one new changeset in the #24813 shape; the card's pending changesets, falsified sentences only — the refusal-status note is untouched. No `packages/spec/**`, no workflow, no other region of auth-plugin.ts, no generated bundle. Held.
- Routed to the seat (not blockers): the class-b finding on the stored select's two unwritten declared values, and the legacy-row / update-path reading (both in the PR's Acceptance notes and the rework note `6307609026`); and the 18.0.0 tag-versus-CHANGELOG observation in ① 7.
- **Check-runs on `48857fcc6`** (47 runs, two workflow runs on the same head):
